subject: pcount vs. multinomPois for removal sampling

messages.author: 985e455b8390aae3
messages.subject: pcount vs. multinomPois for removal sampling
parts:
I was intending to use pcount to estimate relative abundance of
invasive Brown Treesnakes from multiple sites on Guam (Andy, I'm sure
you'll recall working with my colleague Amy Yackel Adams).

We visit each site multiple (many, many) times. The few snakes we
find are removed. Our detection rates are so low with respect to our
expectations of snake density, and surveys occur over extended periods
of time, so I was willing to make the assumption that our removals did
not influence N in any meaningful way.

I've just come across the multinomPois option with type="removal"...it
seems I should be using this, right? However, we have as many as 500
searches at a single site (the vast majority resulting in no snake
observations)...can this function "handle" a multinomial with 500 cell
probabilities?

Shane Siers
Graduate Student
Colorado State University

messages.author: 681fb59733e01a1e
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] pcount vs. multinomPois for removal sampling
parts:
hi Shane,
 Yes, I know her and I'm pretty familiar with this study too , I think she was here for the last workshop. Coincidentally we're covering "unmarked" at our workshop in 2 weeks and we'll talk a lot about these multinomial mixture models.
 Anyhow,  I think the multinomPois() function will work for this no matter how many removals there are -- it uses the Poisson formulation of the marginal likelihood and so it is extremely efficient.
The more general function is gmultmix()   which also fits a type of "open" models and alternative distributions for N (see Chandler et al. 2011; Ecology).
 
 Richard has also been working on more general types of open models which will come to unmarked relatively soon I think.
 
regards
andy
